Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the agreed next steps:

- Redwood ask: We'll run a representative latency/throughput bench against the model variant we discussed and share p50/p95/p99 numbers, token/sec, and guidance for batching/quantization tradeoffs.

Ethan (cc) will share the benchmark results and raw run logs within a couple of days. After that, proposed next steps:

Subject: RE: Post-call recap: latency benchmarks & next steps (Acme)

Hi all —

Attached are the benchmark results from a representative run we executed on 1x A10G (prod-like) with your sample prompt set and the model variant we discussed. High-level summary:

- Test configuration: 1x A10G, model=redwood-base-7b-quant, sequence=512 tokens average, 5 concurrent requests, no batching except internal micro-batching in runtime.
- p50 latency: 45 ms / token
- p95 latency: 120 ms / token
- p99 latency: 210 ms / token
- End-to-end response p95 (including network + runtime overhead): ~280 ms for a 512-token completion
- Throughput: ~22 tokens/sec sustained per GPU under the test pattern (see notes for concurrency scaling)
- Notes: Quantized variant shows ~1.6x improvement in tokens/sec vs fp16 with ~1–2% quality delta for your prompts. Prefix caching wasn't leveraged in this run; enabling it for repeated contexts would decrease perceived latency for repeated patterns.

Caveats and recommendations:
- If your p95 SLO target is <200 ms end-to-end at that token length, we recommend a dedicated pool sized to your QPS peak or enabling aggressive caching + batching in front of hosted endpoints.
- For bursty traffic, a small dedicated capacity with autoscale and a warmed KV cache gives the most consistent p95.

I've attached: acme_latency_benchmarks_20260225.pdf (summary + graphs) and redwood_latency_patchnotes.txt (test harness details). Raw run logs and the k6 script are available here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1-example-bench-run

Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the numbers — Marissa, can you propose 15 minutes with Jordan/Samira next week?

Thanks,
Ethan Park
Applied ML / Inference Engineering
ethan.park@redwood.com
